correctness.rationale: For each b>=1 the first-two-zeros criterion is proved for the doubled word. value.rationale: An exact minimal quotient classification is a natural invariant for a fixed-binary principal superword/subsequence ideal under the standard square-root operation. The closed quadratic count compared with original linear count is a genuine parametric complexity separation, not an arbitrary cutoff or simple restatement of generic upper bounds. The first/second-zero contrast explains the quotient geometry and supplies a usable explicit machine. No claim of a worst-case bound is made.
